prompt: Why does the lesson use margin rather than price to value a customer?

choices.text: Because price changes every month for most of the subscribers
choices.why: Faro's average price is stable; that is not the reason.

choices.text: Because finance forbids analysts from quoting revenue in any presentation
choices.why: No such rule.

choices.text: Because price includes taxes the company has to pass on
choices.why: Not the reason given.

choices.text: Margin is what is left
choices.why: After food, packaging and shipping, margin is what pays for everything else.

prompt: To the centavo, how much margin does one Faro box leave, in reais?
Why is every early cancellation "a customer bought at a loss"?

choices.text: They pay about 1.6 boxes, short of the 2.6 needed to repay the R$ 152
choices.why: R$ 94.19 of margin against R$ 152 of acquisition.

choices.text: They get a refund
choices.why: No refund is mentioned.

choices.text: They never pay
choices.why: They pay 1.6 boxes on average.

choices.text: Shipping is free for them
choices.why: Not in the lesson.

prompt: What it costs to win one new customer is called customer ___ cost.
A customer past 90 days leaves at 4% a month. How many months does the lesson say a survivor stays in total?
hint: Three, plus one over the monthly rate.

prompt: Which assumption does the 28-month figure rest on?

choices.text: That each customer stays exactly 28 months
choices.why: It is an average; some stay far longer, some far less.

choices.text: That the 4% monthly rate stays constant
choices.why: Finance should confirm it before the number reaches a board slide.

choices.text: That price never changes
choices.why: Price is not in the formula.

choices.text: That CAC is R$ 152
choices.why: CAC is not in the formula.

prompt: To one decimal place, what is Faro's LTV-to-CAC ratio for a customer who survives?
Why should the unit-economics formulas sit in a file beside the data?
hint: Renata asks where R$ 1,554 came from.

choices.text: Because spreadsheets calculate faster than a person does in a meeting
choices.why: Speed is not the point.

choices.text: Because auditors require every number to be stored in a spreadsheet
choices.why: No such requirement is mentioned.

choices.text: So the answer is a file she opens
choices.why: A file she can check is stronger than any sentence.

choices.text: For backup
choices.why: Not the reason.

prompt: Trace Faro's driver tree from the finding up to the top.
Why is the first box a short, steep branch of the tree?

choices.text: Because first boxes are the most expensive to ship, so their cost weighs more
choices.why: Shipping cost is not what makes it steep.

choices.text: Because logistics reports it every single day on the dashboard
choices.why: Reporting frequency is not steepness.

choices.text: It decides whether a customer stays
choices.why: A small leaf with a large effect on how long a customer stays.

choices.text: It is a big share
choices.why: It is one delivery in twenty-two.

prompt: You cannot connect your finding to the top of the tree in four or five steps. What does the lesson conclude?

choices.text: That you need finance's full model before you can present anything at all
choices.why: A useful tree needs no finance model.

choices.text: That driver trees do not work for this kind of business
choices.why: They work for any business with a number at the top.

choices.text: That the tree should be drawn with more levels until it connects
choices.why: Padding the tree hides the problem.

choices.text: Too small, or not yet understood
choices.why: Either the finding barely matters to the company, or you have not seen how it does.

prompt: Why is the R$ 77,520 of acquisition not added to the R$ 792,611 of margin?

choices.text: Summing them pretends the marketing spend would have earned as well
choices.why: Both are real; they answer different questions for different readers.

choices.text: It is too small to matter
choices.why: Size is not the reason.

choices.text: Marketing owns it
choices.why: Ownership is part of it, not the reason.

choices.text: It is a one-off
choices.why: It recurs every year.

prompt: How many extra early cancellations a half-year does Calc give from 1,058 late boxes and the 24.1-point gap?
Somebody computes 510 × 28 months × R$ 189.90 ≈ R$ 2.7 million as the loss. What is wrong?

choices.text: It is fine: the more complete version of the same number
choices.why: It counts money Faro would have spent on food and shipping.

choices.text: It uses revenue instead of margin
choices.why: Most of that revenue would have paid for the boxes themselves.

choices.text: 28 months is too long
choices.why: 28 is the lesson's own estimate.

choices.text: It should be monthly
choices.why: Period is not the error.

prompt: Which assumptions does the R$ 790 thousand rest on? Choose all that apply.
hint: Each is a place a sceptic can push.

choices.text: The gap is caused by the delay
choices.why: Step 1 depends on it.

choices.text: Churn after 90 days stays at 4% a month
choices.why: The 28 months depends on it.

choices.text: The margin rate stays at 31%
choices.why: Food and shipping costs move.

choices.text: Ligeiro raises its prices
choices.why: Not part of the calculation.

prompt: Doubling six months to get a year is fine for Faro. When would it not be?

choices.text: When the company has more than one region and they behave differently
choices.why: Regions do not stop a stable pattern from doubling.

choices.text: When the months are reported in a different currency from the year
choices.why: Not a real concern here.

choices.text: For a seasonal business
choices.why: Faro's monthly pattern is stable; a seasonal one is not.

choices.text: Never
choices.why: It fails when the pattern moves through the year.

prompt: Match each term to its trap.

pairs.right: Quoted as if the company kept it

prompt: Before putting a financial number on a slide, what does the lesson tell you to do?
hint: Every company defines these slightly differently.

choices.text: Round it to one significant figure
choices.why: Rounding is lesson 8's subject, and it is not the step named here.

choices.text: Ask finance which definition the company uses
choices.why: A number computed your way beside theirs becomes the conversation.

choices.text: Convert it to dollars
choices.why: No.

choices.text: Leave it out
choices.why: Money is what makes the finding matter.

prompt: What is gross margin?

choices.text: Revenue minus the direct cost of what was sold
choices.why: For Faro, 31% of the price.

choices.text: Profit after taxes
choices.why: That is much further down.

choices.text: Cash in the bank
choices.why: That is cash.

choices.text: What customers pay
choices.why: That is revenue.

prompt: Renata says she does not believe the R$ 790 thousand. What does the lesson suggest saying?

choices.text: That the number was checked by Diego and is therefore correct beyond doubt
choices.why: An appeal to authority, and the assumptions are still assumptions.

choices.text: That the revenue figure of R$ 2.7 million is the more accurate one to use
choices.why: That is the revenue mistake.

choices.text: That it is only an estimate and so not worth debating in the meeting
choices.why: Dismissing it loses the money argument.

choices.text: Which assumption do you doubt?
choices.why: It turns disbelief into a conversation about one assumption, with numbers.
